newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan refugees from Tanzanian camps enter Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees from Tanzanian camps enter Uganda.

text.p: A group of Rwandan refugees crossed into Uganda from Tanzania after escaping from refugee camps to avoid repatriation, U.N. sources said on Thursday.
The group of 559 refugees crossed the Kagera river on the border by private canoe and went to the refugee camp at Oruchinga, about two km (one mile) inside Uganda, they said.

The refugees were part of a larger group that broke out of Karagwe camp earlier this week after Tanzania and the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR announced that Rwandan refugees in Tanzania must go home by the end of the month.

Altogether at least 45,000 refugees have slipped out of camps in Tanzania in the past week. Aid workers say that extremist Hutu militiamen in the camps have been putting pressure on them not to go home.
A UNHCR official in the Ugandan capital Kampala said the agency was sending a protection mission to the Ugandan-Tanzanian border area on Thursday to see the refugees who have crossed.
Many of the other refugees have gone off into the Tanzanian bush. The Tanzanian army is force in the area around the camps but it has not yet taken any action.
The Orunchinga camp already held 5,000 Rwandan Hutu moderates who left the country between 1992 and 1994.
